questions.text: A startup needs computing power, storage, and networking but does not want to buy or maintain its own hardware. Which term best describes the delivery model it should use?
questions.explanation: Cloud computing delivers computing services such as servers, storage, and networking over the internet on a pay-as-you-go basis, so the customer does not own or maintain the physical infrastructure.
questions.source: Original AI-fleet-authored content with publisher review (Dimitri Meier); facts from Microsoft Learn, retrieved 2026-10-02

questions.text: Which characteristic describes the consumption-based model of cloud services?
options: You must buy fixed capacity in advance.
You are billed the same amount every month regardless of use.
You pay only for the resources you use.
You always pay a fixed up-front hardware cost.
questions.explanation: In a consumption-based model you pay only for what you use and you stop incurring charges when you stop using the resources. Buying fixed capacity up front is capital expenditure, not consumption-based pay-as-you-go.
questions.source: Original AI-fleet-authored content with publisher review (Dimitri Meier); facts from Microsoft Learn, retrieved 2026-10-02

questions.text: Under the shared responsibility model, which party is always responsible for the physical security of the cloud datacenter?
options: both the customer and the provider equally
questions.explanation: The shared responsibility model assigns responsibility for the physical security of datacenters, hosts, and networks to the cloud provider. The customer remains responsible for its data, endpoints, accounts, and access management.
questions.source: Original AI-fleet-authored content with publisher review (Dimitri Meier); facts from Microsoft Learn, retrieved 2026-10-02

questions.text: A retail website doubles the number of virtual machines running its storefront during a holiday sale, then reduces them afterward. Which cloud benefit does this describe?
questions.explanation: Scalability is the ability to add or remove resources to meet changing demand, such as scaling out during peak traffic and scaling back in afterward.
